requests: The hero opening has no expressions, so it cannot give a figure answer. It needs {pct(CONTRIBUTIONS_TAX_RATE)}, FY{SITE_CONFIG.financialYear} and {formatAUD(CAP)} rendered in the intro so the opening can state the contributions tax rate, the financial year and the concessional cap directly.

The page has no calculator of its own (its AUDIT intent is lookup-rate-table). The scenario table is fixed at the 30% bracket. A bracket selector, or extra rows for 37% and 45% computed from TAX_BRACKETS, would answer the query for the brackets the text says matter most.

Typed figures in JSX prose (15%, 45%, 60, 22 to 32 cents, $12,000, 2c, the 30% bracket range) should come from constants such as TAX_BRACKETS, CONTRIBUTIONS_TAX_RATE, PRESERVATION_AGE_TABLE and MEDICARE_LEVY so they cannot drift.

The opening paragraph (line 42) has no expression, so it cannot give the direct figure. Add {WFH_CENTS} cents per hour and {RETURN_2026.incomeYear} to the intro so the centerpiece states the 2025-26 fixed rate in its first two sentences.

The page has no WFH calculator of its own. The callout links to the Tax Return Estimator, which takes one total 'Estimated Deductions' figure, not WFH hours. An hours x WFH_CENTS input on this page would match the calculate intent.
The AUDIT centerpiece score is 1.85, but the page opening is not in this FAQ unit. Rewrite the definition and opening in app/notice-of-assessment (or its module) in a separate unit.

The opening could state the income year dates (RETURN_2026.incomeYearStart to RETURN_2026.incomeYearEnd), but those expressions are not in the hero text, so they were not added. Add them in code if wanted.
Replace the hardcoded '2 weeks' at line 74 with {RETURN_2026.onlineRefundTypical} so it matches the hero.

The top query is 'casual to permanent conversion calculator' but the page has no calculator, only a fixed $30/hr table (format_fit 1.83). Add inputs for base rate, weekly hours and paid weeks that run compareCasualToPermanent, near the top of the page.

The opening cannot name the start date of the employee choice pathway because {EMPLOYEE_CHOICE.startDate} is not in the PageHeader text. It also cannot give the break-even figure because {c.breakEvenWeeks} is not there either. Add both expressions to the intro paragraph so the centerpiece can state them.

The intent is lookup-rate-table, but the header intro (line 54) has no rendered figure. To give a direct numeric answer, the opening needs an expression such as {formatAUD(EX_REFUND)} from the worked example or {formatAUD(LITO.maxOffset)}. This needs a code change.

Em dashes remain because they sit in locked short JSX strings: line 103 (' — the ' after the EX_REFUND <strong>) and line 225 (both '—' around the FTL penalty <strong>). These need a code-level edit, using a full stop at line 103 and brackets at line 225.
